Annotation layers for polyviz charts

annotations.Rd

Small builder functions for the objects pv_annotate() accepts: pv_hline() and pv_vline() draw dashed reference lines across the plot, pv_band() shades a region behind the data, and pv_note() places a short text label at a data position, with an optional leader line when it is nudged away from its anchor.

Usage

pv_hline(at, label = NULL, color = NULL)

pv_vline(at, label = NULL, color = NULL)

pv_band(x0 = NULL, x1 = NULL, y0 = NULL, y1 = NULL, label = NULL)

pv_note(x, y, text, dx = 0, dy = 0)

Arguments

at

Where the reference line crosses its axis: a y value for pv_hline(), an x value for pv_vline().

label

Optional short text drawn next to the line or inside the band.

color

Optional line/label colour. NULL (default) uses the theme's secondary ink, which is the right choice almost always - reference lines should recede, not compete with the data.

x0, x1

Both ends of a vertical band on the x axis.

y0, y1

Both ends of a horizontal band on the y axis. Give exactly one pair - x0+x1 or y0+y1, never both.

x, y

Data position the note points at.

text

The note's text. Keep it short - it is drawn on the chart, not in a tooltip.

dx, dy

Pixel offset of the text from its anchor point. When either is non-zero, a thin leader line connects text and anchor.

Value

An annotation object to pass to pv_annotate().

Details

Positions are given in data units. Date values are converted to the ISO strings the charts use internally, and category values (say a bar chart's category name) pass through the axis scale unchanged, so pv_vline("Luzern") works as well as pv_vline(100).

Examples

f25 <- subset(pv_fiscal, year == 2025)
pv_scatter(f25, x = "resource_index", y = "equalization_chf") |>
  pv_annotate(pv_vline(100, label = "cantonal average"),
              pv_band(x0 = 36, x1 = 100))
